KeysToEntries.LensFlare:
Lens flare is a graphical effect that simulates the appearance of bright light sources refracting and scattering within the camera lens. 

This effect creates a realistic and immersive sense of depth and dimensionality in the game's environment, as well as enhancing the overall visual appeal of the game.
KeysToEntries.Resolution:
In Windowed mode, the size of the window is determined by the Display Resolution. 

In Fullscreen mode, the graphics card output resolution is determined by the Display Resolution, which may cause black bars to appear depending on the monitor and graphics card used. 

Display Resolution does not apply to Windowed Fullscreen mode.
KeysToEntries.RenderingMode:
DirectX 11 is an older graphics API (Application Programming Interface)

DirectX 12 is a more recent graphics API that has the potential to provide better performance than DirectX 11. It is necessary to utilize Nanite Virtualized Geometry and Lumen features.
KeysToEntries.PostProcessing:
Post Processing effects such as Motion Blur, Depth of Field, and Bloom can enhance the visual quality of a game's graphics. 

Adjusting the Post Processing quality setting to a higher value can improve the fidelity of these effects, but at the cost of reduced performance.
KeysToEntries.Reflections:
Reflection quality refers to the level of detail and precision in the reflections rendered within the game's environment. It determines the resolution and accuracy of the reflections, creating a more realistic and immersive enviroment.

Off: Reflections are turned off.

Screen Space reflections is a rendering technique that calculates reflections based on the objects currently visible on the screen. It's an efficient way to produce real-time reflections without the need for complex and computationally expensive ray-tracing

Lumen High/Epic is a high-quality real-time ray-tracing technique that produces accurate reflections by tracing rays of light in real-time. This technique is much more computationally expensive than Screen Space reflections, but it offers a higher level of visual fidelity and realism.
KeysToEntries.GlobalIllumination:
Global Illumination is a rendering technique that simulates the way light bounces around and interacts with the environment in the game, affecting the quality and distribution of ambient lighting.

Off: Fully dynamic illumination

On: Fully dynamic global illumination
KeysToEntries.Bloom:
Bloom is a post-processing effect that simulates the way bright lights appear to bleed into their surroundings, creating a glowing halo or aura around the light source. Creating a more visually stunning and cinematic enviroment, enhancing the overall atmosphere and immersion.

Off: There is no additional post-processing applied to the lighting effects, resulting in a more realistic and muted look.

On: The game applies a post-processing effect to the lighting, resulting in a more intense and stylized look.
KeysToEntries.V-Sync:
V-Sync (Vertical Synchronization) can help eliminate screen tearing, which occurs when the graphics card and monitor are out of sync. Screen tearing can cause visual artifacts and distortion on the screen, making the game look choppy and unpleasant to play.

When V-Sync is enabled, the game's frame rate is synchronized with the refresh rate of the monitor. This means that the graphics card only sends a new frame to the monitor once it has completed rendering the previous one. This synchronization helps to eliminate screen tearing and provides a smoother, more stable visual experience.

However, enabling V-Sync can also introduce some input lag, as the game may have to wait for the next monitor refresh cycle before registering player input. This can result in a slight delay between the player's actions and the response of the game.
KeysToEntries.FrameRateLimit:
Frame Rate Limit can be used to cap the maximum frame rate of the game. A higher frame rate can result in smoother and more responsive gameplay, but it also requires more processing power and can cause more heat generation and noise from the computer's hardware.

By setting a Frame Rate Limit, the game's frame rate is capped at a specific value, which can help ensure that the game runs smoothly without taxing the computer's hardware too much. This can help to reduce the risk of overheating, fan noise, and other hardware-related issues.

This feature only works in Fullscreen mode.
KeysToEntries.WindowedMode:
Fullscreen mode the game takes over the entire screen and runs in exclusive mode. In fullscreen mode, the game has direct access to the graphics hardware and can achieve maximum performance and visual quality.

Windowed mode is an alternative display mode that allows the game to run in a window on the desktop, similar to any other application. In windowed mode, the game is not running in exclusive mode and is sharing system resources with other applications. This can impact performance and visual quality.

Borderless windowed mode (also known as fullscreen windowed mode or windowed fullscreen) is a hybrid display mode that combines the benefits of fullscreen mode and windowed mode. In borderless windowed mode, the game runs in a maximized window that covers the entire desktop, but without a border or title bar. This creates the appearance of fullscreen mode, but with the added benefit of being able to quickly switch between the game and other applications using alt-tab or other methods.
KeysToEntries.AATSR:
Both Anti-Aliasing and Super Resolution can help smooth jagged edges and stabilize images during motion. However, Super Resolution takes performance improvement even further by rendering fewer pixels per frame to achieve the same output resolution.

OFF: Anti-Aliasing is completely turned off.

FXAA: Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing is a cost-effective way to reduce jagged edges, but its spatial-only anti-aliasing method may cause flickering.

TAA: Temporal Anti-Aliasing provides superior quality compared to FXAA by leveraging information from both previous frames and the current frame.

TSR Low/Medium/High/Epic: Temporal Super Resolution is a technique that can improve anti-aliasing quality and overall rendering performance by rendering fewer pixels per frame while producing visually comparable output imagery
KeysToEntries.Shadows: The level of shadow detail impacts the clarity and range of moving shadows. Shadows enhance visual fidelity and enhance spatial perception, but may come at the cost of performance. When Nanite technology is utilized, Virtual Shadow Maps will be employed to achieve even greater fidelity.
KeysToEntries.Effects: Controls the level of visual effects in the game, with higher settings yielding better quality effects but potentially impacting performance.
KeysToEntries.Textures: Higher texture quality means flat objects will display a more intricate appearance. However, increasing this setting may result in decreased performance.
KeysToEntries.Clouds:
How the clouds are displayed in the enviroment.

Static: Emulates the appearance of volumetric clouds using a static cloud texture, incurring significantly lower performance cost than Volumetric Clouds.

2D Dynamic: Basic 2D Cloud texture with dynamic movement.

Volumetric: Utilizes a 3D Volumetric Cloud system, generating a more lifelike sky effect but with a performance trade-off.
KeysToEntries.ViewDistance: This determines how far away an object can be before it is culled. This has a performance trade-off.
KeysToEntries.Foliage: Quality of foliage in the enviroment, Higher quality foliage has a more realistic and immersive enviroment but may impact performance.
KeysToEntries.3DResolution:
Governs the rendering resolution of in-game objects. Decreasing this setting can boost the frame rate but also reduce visual quality.

Warning this is controlled by DLSS/FIDELITY if enabled.
KeysToEntries.Materials: Determines the quality of materials in the enviroment, Can have some positive performance impacts when lowered.
KeysToEntries.Nanite:
Nanite uses a new approach to rendering that enables the game engine to dynamically stream in only the necessary level of detail for each object and surface based on the user's viewpoint, resulting in highly-detailed and expansive environments.

This is achieved by leveraging hardware-accelerated virtual texturing, which allows textures to be streamed and rendered on-demand, reducing memory usage while preserving visual fidelity.
KeysToEntries.MotionBlur: Motion blur can enhance the look of animations and the environment
KeysToEntries.HardwareRayTracing: Uses Hardware Ray Tracing for Lumen features when supported by the video card, RHI, and operating system. Lumen will fall back to Software Ray Tracing otherwise. Hardware Ray Tracing is designed for modern GPUs
KeysToEntries.NvidiaDLSS:
NVIDIA DLSS leverages AI and machine learning with NVIDIA’s GPUs to upscale resolution for better looking graphics with reduced computational load.

OFF: Disables Nvidia's DLSS.

DLAA: Focuses solely on using DLSS to improve image quality without upscaling, this gives the highest visual fidelity over performance.

QUALITY: Provides a balanced approach with slight trade off in image quality for performance.

BALANCED: Prioritizes a balance between performance and image quality.

PERFORMANCE: Prioritizes high frame rates, making minor sacrifices in image quality.

ULTRA PERFORMANCE: Maximizes performance by significantly lowering the rendering resolution before applying DLSS upscaling.
KeysToEntries.NVIDIAFG:
NVIDIA Frame Generation utilizes the power of AI to analyze and predict motion between frames more accurately. This allows for the creation of new frames that seamlessly blend with the original ones, reducing stutter and improving the overall smoothness of motion without a noticeable impact on visual fidelity.

Off: Disabled Nvidia Frame Generation.

On: Activates Nvidia Frame Generation providing constant boost in performance.

Auto: Nvidia Frame Generation will automatically be toggled on and off based on performance.
KeysToEntries.AMDFSR:
AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 3

Native AA: Uses Super Resolution to perform temporal anti-aliasing without upscaling.

Quality: Produces a Super Resolution image which is nearly indiscernible from native rendering, and should be selected when image fidelity is paramount.

Balanced: Produces a Super Resolution image which is representative of native rendering, with minimal artifacts and sizeable performance gains.

Performance: Produces a Super Resolution image which approximates native rendering, with occasional artifacts but exceptional performance gains.

Ultra Performance: Produces a Super Resolution image which may have notable artifacts under some conditions, and should be selected in situations where performance is critical.
KeysToEntries.ShadowSmoothing:
WARNING: This is GPU-intensive and may reduce frame rates or increase graphical load, particularly on lower-end systems. Adjust this setting based on your preference for visual fidelity versus performance.

This setting enhances the visual quality of shadows by smoothing the transition and update intervals. Enabling this feature results in more realistic and less distracting shadow movements.
